data.text: The uuid package generates RFC 4122 version 1, 4, and 5 UUIDs for browser and Node.js.

data.title: Generate UUIDs

data.text: The `uuid` package generates RFC-compliant UUIDs. `v4()` is random, `v7()` is time-ordered so it sorts by creation time and indexes better, and `v5()` derives a deterministic UUID from a name and namespace. The `crypto.randomUUID()` built into modern runtimes covers the common v4 case without any dependency.

data.title: v4 and v7 identifiers

data.text: A random v4 primary key inserts into a B-tree in unpredictable order, causing page splits and index bloat. A v7 key begins with a timestamp, so new rows append near the end of the index and remain roughly sequential. That is the same reasoning behind UUID versus auto-increment integer keys in a database schema.

data.title: A time-ordered primary key
UUID vs auto-increment
data.text: A UUID is safe to generate on the client, does not leak row counts, and lets many services create ids without coordination. An integer is smaller and index-friendly. The modern middle ground is a time-ordered UUID such as v7, which keeps the distributed benefits and recovers most of the index locality. Say that rather than presenting one as universally correct.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: UUID v4 is random and collision-resistant.
Use for database IDs and keys.
